C. New Technology APCs
1. Background
In the CY 2002 OPPS final rule (
66 FR 59903
), we finalized changes to the time period in which a service can be eligible for payment under a New Technology APC. Beginning in CY 2002, we retain services within New Technology APC groups until we gather sufficient claims data to enable us to assign the service to an appropriate clinical APC. This policy allows us to move a service from a New Technology APC in less than 2 years if sufficient data are available. It also allows us to retain a service in a New Technology APC for more than 2 years if sufficient data upon which to base a decision for reassignment have not been collected.
We also adopted in the CY 2002 OPPS final rule the following criteria for assigning a complete or comprehensive service to a New Technology APC: (1) the service must be truly new, meaning it cannot be appropriately reported by an existing HCPCS code assigned to a clinical APC and does not appropriately fit within an existing clinical APC; (2) the service is not eligible for transitional pass-through payment (however, a truly new, comprehensive service could qualify for assignment to a new technology APC even if it involves a device or drug that could, on its own, qualify for pass-through payment); and (3) the service falls within the scope of Medicare benefits under section 1832(a) of the Act and is reasonable and necessary in accordance with section 1862(a)(1)(A) of the Act (
66 FR 59898
through
59903
). For additional information about our New Technology APC policy, we refer readers to
https://www.cms.gov/​medicare/​payment/​prospective-payment-systems/​hospital-outpatient/​pass-through-payment-status-new-technology-ambulatory-payment-classification-apc
on the CMS website and then follow the instructions to access the MEARIS
TM
system for OPPS New Technology APC applications.
[
15
]
In the CY 2004 OPPS final rule with comment period (
68 FR 63416
), we restructured the New Technology APCs to make the cost intervals more consistent across payment levels and refined the cost bands for these APCs to retain two parallel sets of New Technology APCs: one set with a status indicator of “S” (Significant Procedures, Not Discounted when Multiple. Paid under OPPS; separate APC payment) and the other set with a status indicator of “T” (Significant Procedure, Multiple Reduction Applies. Paid under OPPS; separate APC payment). These current New Technology APC configurations allow us to price new technology services more appropriately and consistently.
For CY 2026, there were 52 New Technology APC levels, ranging from the lowest cost band assigned to APC 1491 (New Technology—Level 1A ($0- $10)) to the highest cost band assigned to APC 1908 (New Technology—Level 52 ($145,001-$160,000)). We note that the cost bands for the New Technology APCs, specifically, APCs 1491 through 1599 and 1901 through 1908, vary with increments ranging from $10 to $14,999. These cost bands identify the APCs to
(
printed page 70366)
which new technology procedures and services with estimated service costs that fall within those cost bands are assigned under the OPPS. Payment for each APC is made at the mid-point of the APC's assigned cost band. For example, payment for APC 1507 (New Technology—Level 7 ($501-$600)) is made at $550.50.
Under the OPPS, one of our goals is to make payments that are appropriate for the services that are necessary for the treatment of Medicare beneficiaries. The OPPS, like other Medicare payment systems, is intended to be budget neutral in comparison to what would have been paid under the previous reasonable-cost payment system, and increases are limited to the annual hospital market basket increase reduced by the productivity adjustment. We believe that our payment rates reflect the costs that are associated with providing care to Medicare beneficiaries and continue to be adequate to ensure access to services. For many emerging technologies, there is a transitional period during which utilization may be low, often because providers are first learning about the technologies and their clinical utility. Quite often, parties request that Medicare make higher payments under the New Technology APCs for new procedures in that transitional phase. These requests, and their accompanying estimates for expected total patient utilization, often reflect very low rates of patient use of expensive equipment, resulting in high per-use costs for which requesters believe Medicare should make full payment. Medicare does not, and we believe should not, assume responsibility for more than its share of the costs of procedures based on projected utilization for Medicare beneficiaries and does not set its payment rates based on initial projections of low utilization for services that require expensive capital equipment. For the OPPS, we rely on hospitals to make informed business decisions regarding the acquisition of high-cost capital equipment, taking into consideration their knowledge about their entire patient base (Medicare beneficiaries included) and an understanding of Medicare's and other payers' payment policies. We refer readers to the CY 2013 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (
77 FR 68314
) for further discussion regarding this payment policy.
Some services assigned to New Technology APCs have low annual volume, which we consider to be fewer than 100 claims in the year of claims data used for ratesetting (
86 FR 63528
). Where utilization of services assigned to a New Technology APC is low, it can lead to wide variation in payment rates from year to year, resulting in even lower utilization and potential barriers to access of new technologies, which ultimately limits our ability to assign the service to the appropriate clinical APC. To mitigate these issues, we finalized a policy in the CY 2019 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period to utilize our equitable adjustment authority at section 1833(t)(2)(E) of the Act to adjust how we determine the costs for low-volume services assigned to New Technology APCs (
83 FR 58892
through
58893
). Specifically, in the CY 2019 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (
83 FR 58893
), we established that, in each of our annual rulemakings, we would calculate and present the result of each statistical methodology (arithmetic mean, geometric mean, and median) based on up to 4 years of claims data and solicit public comment on which methodology should be used to establish the payment rate for the low-volume new technology service. However, in the CY 2022 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (
86 FR 63529
), we replaced the New Technology APC low volume policy with the universal low volume APC policy. Unlike the discontinued New Technology APC low volume policy, the universal low volume APC policy applies to clinical APCs and brachytherapy APCs, in addition to procedures assigned to New Technology APCs, and uses the highest of the geometric mean, arithmetic mean, or median based on up to 4 years of claims data to set the payment rate for the APC. We refer readers to the CY 2022 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (
86 FR 63529
) for further discussion regarding this policy.
Despite the universal low volume APC policy, we continued to see payment instability for services with very low claims volume of fewer than 10 claims in the 4-year lookback period used under the universal low volume APC policy. For CY 2025, we finalized a policy to exempt services assigned to New Technology APCs with fewer than 10 claims over the 4-year lookback period used for the universal low volume policy. Instead of assigning these services to a different New Technology APC based on the very few claims available, we maintained the New Technology APC assignment for each service from the prior year, CY 2024. We refer readers to the CY 2025 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period for a discussion on the policy (
89 FR 94016

91 FR 41791
).
In the CY 2026 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period we finalized a continuation of the policy to exempt services assigned to New Technology APCs with fewer than 10 claims over the 4-year lookback period from the universal low volume policy moving forward. We finalized to continue this policy in future years, until, or unless, an alternative policy was finalized. We refer readers to the CY 2026 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period for a discussion on the policy (
90 FR 53530
through

In addition to the universal low volume policy and the policy to exempt services with fewer than 10 claims in the 4-year lookback period, it has been our policy to maintain the New Technology APC assignment for services with zero claims in the claims year used for rulemaking. For CY 2027, since we proposed CY 2027 OPPS payment rates based on CY 2025 claims data, if a service has no CY 2025 claims, we proposed to maintain the same New Technology APC assignment for CY 2027 (

Finally, we note that, in a budget-neutral system, payments may not fully cover hospitals' costs in a particular circumstance, including those for the purchase and maintenance of capital equipment. We rely on hospitals to make their decisions regarding the acquisition of high-cost equipment with the understanding that the Medicare program must be careful to establish its initial payment rates, including those made through New Technology APCs, for new services that lack hospital claims data based on realistic utilization projections for all such services delivered in cost-efficient hospital

f. Supervised Visits for Esketamine Self- Administration (APCs 1513 and 1517)
On March 5, 2019, FDA approved SPRAVATO® (esketamine) nasal spray, used in conjunction with an oral antidepressant for treatment of depression in adults who have tried other antidepressant medicines but have not benefited from them (treatment-resistant depression (TRD)). This is the first FDA approval of esketamine for any use.
Esketamine is a noncompetitive N- methyl D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonist. It is a nasal spray supplied as an aqueous solution of esketamine hydrochloride in a vial with a nasal spray device. Each device delivers two sprays containing a total of 28 mg of esketamine. Patients would require either two (2) devices (for a 56 mg dose) or three (3) devices (for an 84 mg dose) per treatment.
Because of the risk of serious adverse outcomes resulting from sedation and dissociation and respiratory depression caused by esketamine nasal spray administration, and the potential for abuse and misuse of the product, it is only available through a restricted distribution system under a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS). A REMS is a drug safety program that the FDA can require for certain medications with serious safety concerns to help ensure the benefits of the medication outweigh its risks. The SPRAVATO® REMS program requires, among other requirements, that the esketamine nasal spray be dispensed and administered to enrolled patients in health care settings that are certified in the REMS. See
www.fda.gov
for more information regarding the SPRAVATO® REMS program requirements.
A treatment session of esketamine consists of instructed nasal self- administration by the patient followed by a period of at least 2 hours post-administration observation of the patient under direct supervision of a health care professional in the certified health care setting. g. SAINT Neuromodulation System (APCs 1511 and 1525)
The SAINT Neuromodulation System is a non-invasive repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) system that identifies an individualized target and delivers navigationally directed repetitive magnetic pulses to that individualized target located within the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex to treat major depressive disorder (MDD). The patient first receives structural MRI and functional MRI scans that are analyzed by the provider to identify and localize the personalized stimulation target in the patient's dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Once the areas targeted for treatment are identified, the patient receives non-invasive magnetic stimulation in the targeted area. The patient has 10 treatment sessions per day with each treatment session lasting 10 minutes followed by 50 minutes of rest before another treatment session occurs. The treatment is administered over five days for a total of 50 sessions of non-invasive magnetic stimulation therapy. Accelerated, repetitive high-dose functional connectivity MRI-guided theta-burst stimulation, including target assessment, initial motor threshold determination, neuronavigation, delivery and management, initial treatment day.

E. APC-Specific Policies
1. Creation and/or Revisions of Clinical APCs
Neurostimulator and Related Procedures (APCs 5461 Through 5465)
In prior rulemaking, some interested parties have requested that we create a Level 6 Neurostimulator and Related Procedures APC, due to their concerns around clinical and resource cost similarity in the Level 5 Neurostimulator and Related Procedures APC. We most recently responded to this request in the CY 2026 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (
90 FR 53584
). We noted that we believed that the current 5 level APC structure for the Neurostimulator and Related Procedures series provided for an appropriate distribution of clinical and cost similarity at the different APC levels.
As discussed in the CY 2021 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period, we reiterate that the OPPS is a prospective payment system. We group procedures with similar clinical characteristics and resource costs into APCs and establish a payment rate that reflects the geometric mean of all services in the group even though the cost of any individual service within the APC may be higher or lower than the APC's geometric mean. As a result, in the OPPS, any individual procedure may potentially be paid more or less than the cost of the services because the payment rate is based on the geometric mean of the entire group of services in the APC. However, the impact of these payment differences should be mitigated when distributed across a large number of APCs (
85 FR 85968
).
We continued to believe that a five-level structure for the Neurostimulator and Related Procedures APC series remained appropriate, and therefore in the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC proposed rule our proposed assignments for the structure and for many codes in the APC series remained the same as they were in the CY 2026 OPPS/ASC final rule.

We appreciate the thoughtful responses commenters have provided with regard to the Neurostimulator and Related Procedures APC series. At this time, we continue to believe the 5-level APC structure for the APC series remains appropriate and that the individual New Technology APC assignments with respect to the high-cost procedures in this evolving area resolve the concerns around procedure payment relative to cost. Finally, we note that for the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC final rule we are not removing any codes from the IPO list to the Neurostimulator and Related Procedures APC series. We will continue to monitor the claims data for these procedures as more information around their volume and estimated costs become available.
After consideration of public comments, we are finalizing the proposed assignments of CPT codes 33276 and 64568 to New Technology APC 1580, finalizing the proposed assignment of 61885 to APC 5465, and maintaining the 5-level APC structure for the Neurostimulator and Related Procedures APC series for CY 2027.
Laparoscopy and Related Services (APCs 5361 Through 5362)
As part of the CY 2016 OPPS APC restructuring process, the four level APC series for Laparoscopy and Related Services was consolidated into a 2-level APC series (
80 FR 70379
). Since that time, we have maintained that 2- level APC structure based on the clinical and resource homogeneity of the services assigned to those APCs.
Comment:
A commenter noted that several of the codes newly proposed to be removed from the inpatient only list and assigned to the Level 2 Laparaoscopy and Related Services APC have higher geometric mean costs relative to the APC geometric mean cost for this APC, including for CPT codes 32663 (Thoracoscopy, surgical; with lobectomy (single lobe)), 32666 (Thoracoscopy, surgical; with therapeutic wedge resection (
e.g.,
mass, nodule), initial unilateral), and 32669 (Thoracoscopy, surgical; with removal of a single lung segment (segmentectomy)). The commenter requested that CMS consider whether a higher level Laparoscopy and Related Services APC is needed to establish appropriate payment for these services in the outpatient setting.
Response:
While we monitor the structure of the OPPS and the various APCs, we note that some of the principles guiding the CY 2016 OPPS APC restructuring and consolidation included improved resource and clinical homogeneity, as well as reduced resource overlap in APCs within a clinical family (
80 FR 70379
). APC 5362 (Level 2 Laparoscopy and Related Services) has an estimated geometric mean cost of $11,401, with a range of geometric mean costs for two times rule purposes ranging from $9,347 for CPT code 58552 (Laparoscopy, surgical, with vaginal hysterectomy, for uterus 250 g or less; with removal of tube(s) and/or ovary(s)) to $13,534 for CPT code 55866 (Laparoscopy, surgical prostatectomy, retropubic radical, including nerve sparing, includes robotic assistance, when performed). While we recognize the commenter's concern around estimated costs for services removed from the IPO list being assigned to the Laparaoscopy and Related Services APC series, we note that geometric mean costs for CPT codes 32666 and 32669 fall well within that range of significant costs for the APC, and that all three codes have limited outpatient claims volume. We do not believe that there is a current need for an additional APC level for the Laparoscopy and Related Services APC series. However, we will continue to monitor the claims data as more claims become available and consider the need for additional APC levels in the future.
After consideration of the public comments, we are finalizing the 2-level APC structure for the Laparoscopy and Related Services APC series in this final rule with comment period as proposed.
Nuclear Medicine and Related Services APC Series (APC 5591 Through 5594)
The Nuclear Medicine and Related Services APC series was created as part of the broader APC restructuring and consolidation in the CY 2016 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (
80 FR 70392
through
70397
). The APC series was developed from what were previously separate APC groupings primarily organized by anatomy and imaging modality. Since the initial establishment of the Nuclear Medicine and Related Services series in the CY 2016 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period, we have maintained the four-level APC structure for the series.
In the CY 2025 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period, we finalized a policy of paying separately for diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals with estimated per day costs higher than a packaging threshold specific to diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals (
89 FR 93948
through
93963
). Because certain diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals are paid separately under the policy, the nuclear medicine and other services these diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals would otherwise be packaged into would no longer include those costs. As a result, based on the associated changes to the ratesetting process, we observed impacts on the estimated cost of services assigned to the Nuclear Medicine and Related Services APC series such that the range of cost significant codes across the various APC levels became less distinct, in particular between Levels 3 and 4.
As part of our standard process of reviewing updated claims and cost report data, we continued to observe in the CY 2027 OPPS data that the differences between the four levels of APC geometric means were less distinct than they were previously, in part due to the policy of paying separately for diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals. Specifically, under a four-level APC structure using the 2027 NPRM claims data and maintaining the same APC assignments as in the CY 2026 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period, the geometric mean cost of the Level 3 APC would have been $1,367.99 while the geometric mean cost of the Level 4 APC would have been $1,497.06. The range of cost significant codes in the Level 3 APC would have been from $812 to $1,404, while the range for the Level 4 APC would have been from $1,024 to $1,676; indicating a high degree of overlap in the estimated costs of the services assigned to those APC levels. Given the relative proximity of the APC geometric mean costs and the clinical and cost similarities of the services between the APCs in the Nuclear Medicine and Related Services series, we believed that it was appropriate to reorganize the Nuclear Medicine and Related Services APC series for the CY 2027 OPPS (
91 FR 41808
).
Additionally, we noted that CPT codes 78431 (Myocardial imaging, positron emission tomography (pet), perfusion study (including ventricular wall motion[s] and/or ejection fraction[s], when performed); multiple studies at rest and stress (exercise or
(
printed page 70385)
pharmacologic), with concurrently acquired computed tomography transmission scan), 78432 (Myocardial imaging, positron emission tomography (pet), combined perfusion with metabolic evaluation study (including ventricular wall motion[s] and/or ejection fraction[s], when performed), dual radiotracer (e.g., myocardial viability);), and 78433 (Myocardial imaging, positron emission tomography (pet), combined perfusion with metabolic evaluation study (including ventricular wall motion[s] and/or ejection fraction[s], when performed), dual radiotracer (e,g., myocardial viability); with concurrently acquired computed tomography transmission scan) had sufficient CY 2025 claims data available to be appropriately assigned to clinical APCs for CY 2027 OPPS ratesetting. We believed the restructuring of the series now made it appropriate to propose to assign these codes to APC 5594 (Level 4 Nuclear Medicine and Related Services) and we proposed to assign these three CPT codes to APC 5594 for CY 2027 (
91 FR 41808
).
Based on our review of the updated claims data, we proposed to reassign a number of services to revised levels in the Nuclear Medicine and Related Services APC series for CY 2027 and to assign CPT codes 78431, 78432, and 78433 to APC 5594 (Level 4 Nuclear Medicine and Related Services) in the CY 2027 OPPS. Please see the APC- sorted Two Times Listing for the proposed rule on the CMS website or Addendum B to the proposed rule to see the Nuclear Medicine APC we proposed to assign each HCPCS code in the series.
Comment:
Commenters supported the proposed reorganization of the Nuclear Medicine and Related Services APC series and the proposed assignment of PET/CT procedures to APC 5594 (Level 4 Nuclear Medicine and Related Services).
Response:
We appreciate the commenters' support.
Comment:
Two commenters expressed concern regarding the proposed reassignment of CPT code 78830 (Radiopharmaceutical localization of tumor, inflammatory process or distribution of radiopharmaceutical agent(s) (includes vascular flow and blood pool imaging, when performed); tomographic (spect) with concurrently acquired computed tomography (ct) transmission scan for anatomical review, localization and determination/detection of pathology, single area (e.g., head, neck, chest, pelvis) or acquisition, single day imaging) to APC 5592 (Level 2 Nuclear Medicine and Related Services). One of the commenters was concerned that the change would cause a move to more expensive, more invasive tests and that a phased in approach while more claims data continue to be collected.
A commenter expressed concern about the proposed assignment of CPT codes 78075 (Adrenal imaging, cortex and/or medulla), 78454 (Myocardial perfusion imaging, planar (including qualitative or quantitative wall motion, ejection fraction by first pass or gated technique, additional quantification, when performed); multiple studies, at rest and/or stress (exercise or pharmacologic) and/or redistribution and/or rest reinjection), 78811 (Positron emission tomography (pet) imaging; limited area (e.g., chest, head/neck)), and 78831 (Radiopharmaceutical localization of tumor, inflammatory process or distribution of radiopharmaceutical agent(s) (includes vascular flow and blood pool imaging, when performed); tomographic (spect), minimum 2 areas (e.g., pelvis and knees, chest and abdomen) or separate acquisitions (e.g., lung ventilation and perfusion), single day imaging, or single area or acquisition over 2 or more days) to APC 5592 (Level 2 Nuclear Medicine and Related Services) and recommended assignment to APC 5593 (Level 3 Nuclear Medicine and Related Services) instead.
Response:
We understand the commenter's concern. Based on the data in this final rule, the geometric mean costs for these codes range from $746.48 for CPT code 78811 to $899.39 for CPT code 78831. We believe that these codes are more appropriately placed based on their estimated costs in APC 5592, with a geometric mean cost of $591.45 rather than the Level 3 APC 5593, which has an estimated geometric mean cost $1,433.70. Additionally, in reviewing the prior year's claims data, the geometric mean cost for these codes were similarly situated. While we will continue to monitor the claims data for these codes in the future, we do not believe a phased approach is necessary, as they are appropriately assigned to APC 5592 based on the geometric mean cost of these services.
After consideration of the public comments we received, we are finalizing the HCPCS assignments for CPT codes 78075, 78454, 78811, 78830, and 78831 to APC 5592, as proposed.

2. Cochlear Infusion of a Pharmacologic Agent, CPT Code 1056T (APC 5165)
For CY 2027, the AMA CPT Editorial Board created a new Category I CPT code 1056T (Placeholder code X565T) to describe a cochlear infusion procedure required for the administration of OTARMENI
TM
which is the first FDA-approved gene therapy for genetic hearing loss.
Later, the AMA CPT Editorial Board changed the effective date of the CPT code 1056T,
Cochlear infusion of pharmacologic agent (ie, gene therapy vector), including mastoidectomy, labyrinthotomy, and repair of fenestrations,
from January 1, 2027, to October 1, 2026. OTARMENI
TM
is an adeno-associated virus vector-based gene therapy indicated for the treatment of pediatric and adult patients with severe-to-profound and profound sensorineural hearing loss (any frequency >90 dB HL) associated with molecularly confirmed biallelic variants in the
OTOF
gene, preserved outer hair cell function, and no prior cochlear implant in the same ear.
OTARMENI
TM
is administered as a single dose intracochlear infusion. The recommended dose for each ear is 7.2 × 10
12
vector genomes in a total volume of 0.24 ml.
In the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC proposed rule, we proposed to assign CPT code 1056T to SI “J1”, APC 5163 (Level 3 ENT Procedures) with a proposed payment rate of $1,755.96.
We received public comments on this proposal. The following is a summary of the comments we received.
Comment:
The commenters requested that CMS reassign CPT code 1056T from APC 5163 (Level 3 ENT Procedures) to APC 5165 (Level 5 ENT Procedures).
They stated that CPT code 1056T describes a highly specialized surgical procedure that requires significant operative expertise, dedicated training, substantial facility resources, and multidisciplinary coordination. The procedure includes complex otologic surgical components such as mastoidectomy and labyrinthotomy, which are more comparable to higher-acuity ENT procedures than to those typically associated with a Level 3 APC assignment. Because CPT code 1056T includes mastoidectomy as well as additional work associated with intracochlear infusion of a gene therapy vector, the commenters believe that APC 5165 better reflects the resources required to perform the cochlear infusion procedure and represents the most appropriate APC assignment for 1056T.
Commenters also noted that cochlear infusion reported with CPT code 1056T, differs substantially from the procedure described by CPT code 69801 (
Labyrinthotomy, with perfusion of vestibuloactive drug(s), transcanal),
which per our proposed rule review was
(
printed page 70386)
determined to be similar to CPT code 1056T and is assigned to APC 5163. CPT code 1056T describes an open surgical approach that includes mastoidectomy, labyrinthotomy, repair of fenestrations, and intracochlear infusion of a gene therapy vector, whereas CPT code 69801 describes a minimally invasive transcanal drug perfusion procedure that does not include mastoidectomy.
Response:
We appreciate the commenters' feedback on this new CPT code, and we agree with the commenters' recommendation to change the APC assignment for this code. Because CPT code 1056T describes an open surgical approach that includes mastoidectomy, which differs from a minimally invasive transcanal drug perfusion procedure described by CPT code 69801, we now believe that CPT code 1056T is more appropriately assigned to APC 5165 (Level 5 ENT Procedures).
In summary, after consideration of the public comments we received, we are not adopting our proposal as final. Instead, we are assigning CPT code 1056T to APC 5165 (Level 5 ENT Procedures) for CY 2027.
Table 29 shows the finalized status indicator and APC assignment for this procedure code. We refer readers to Addendum B of this final rule with comment period for the payment rates for all codes reportable under the OPPS. Addendum B is available via the internet on the CMS website.

For CY 2027, the AMA CPT Editorial Board created 4 New Category I CPT codes 92513, 92514, 92527 and 92528 (placeholder CPT codes 92X10, 92X11, 92XX5, and 92XX6). These new codes reflect advances in vestibular testing and provide greater specificity for reporting services used by audiologists to evaluate vestibular function.
92513—
Video head impulse testing (vHIT), with recording, interpretation, and report; of lateral semicircular canal function;
92514—
Video head impulse testing (vHIT), with recording, interpretation, and report; of lateral and vertical semicircular canal function;
92527—
Rotational vestibular assessment by sinusoidal harmonic acceleration (SHA) testing with calibrated, computer-controlled chair, with interpretation and report; and
92528—
Rotational vestibular assessment by sinusoidal harmonic acceleration (SHA) testing with calibrated, computer-controlled chair, with interpretation and report; with velocity step testing (VST)
In the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC proposed rule, we proposed to assign CPT codes 92513, 92514, and 92527 to APC 5721 (Level 1 Diagnostic Tests and Related Services) with status indicator “S” and proposed payment rate of $146.93. We proposed to assign CPT code 92528 to status indicator “N”.
Comment:
We received one public comment on this proposal. The commenter supported our assignment of CPT codes 92513, 92514, and 92527 to APC 5721 for CY 2027; however, they were concerned with our proposed assignment of status indicator “N” to CPT code 92528 which would package payment for VST into payment for the base rotational vestibular assessment service (CPT code 92527). The commenter stated that the additional velocity step testing represented by CPT code 92528 requires clinical work and resources beyond those necessary to perform the base SHA testing service represented by CPT code 92527. This, according to the commenter, includes additional provider time and greater work intensity associated with CPT code 92528. The new CPT code family distinguishes the base SHA assessment from the additional VST service. The commenter also recognized our longstanding policy of packaging most procedures described by add-on codes. However, they believed that the distinct resource requirements associated with CPT code 92528 warranted reconsideration.
Response:
We thank the commenter for their feedback. Our medical advisors reviewed the service described by CPT code 92528, and we do not believe that it takes significant additional time or hospital resources to perform this service. Therefore, we concluded that VST service described by an add-on CPT code 92528 is appropriately packaged into the base SHA testing service described by CPT code 92527. This is consistent with our packaging policy outlined at
42 CFR 419.2(b)
, which lists the types of items and services for which payment is packaged under the OPPS. Specifically, certain services described by add-on codes.
Therefore, we believe our proposed assignment of status indicator “N” to CPT code 92528 remains appropriate. As a result, we are finalizing our proposal without modification to assign CPT code 92528 to status indicator “N” for CY 2027.

For CY 2027, we proposed to continue to assign the following cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) CPT codes to APC 5523 (Level 3 Imaging without Contrast), APC 5524 (Level 4 Imaging without Contrast), APC 5572 (Level 2 Imaging with Contrast), and APC 5573 (Level 3 Imaging with Contrast). The codes, long descriptors and payment assignments are listed below.
CPT code 75557—
Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging for morphology and function without contrast material.
CPT code 75557 is currently assigned to APC 5523 (Level 3 Imaging without Contrast) and has a geometric mean cost of $305 based on 1,453 single frequency claims used for ratesetting;
(
printed page 70387)
CPT code 75559—
Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging for morphology and function without contrast material; with stress imaging.
CPT code 7559 is currently assigned to APC 5524 (Level 4 Imaging without Contrast) and has a geometric mean cost of $378, based on 19 single frequency claims used for ratesetting;
CPT code 75561—
Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging for morphology and function without contrast material(s), followed by contrast material(s) and further sequences.

We received one public comment on these codes.
Comment:
The commenter states that our “current modality-based APC structure creates a substantial and increasingly difficult-to-justify payment disparity between clinically comparable advanced cardiac imaging services.” The commenter suggests that contrast-enhanced cardiac MRI (CMR) requires more hospital resources than single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) and positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging and should not be placed in general imaging APCs with/without contrast APCs that also include non-cardiac related imaging examinations requiring very different resources. According to the commenter, the payment for SPECT and PET is influenced by advanced cardiac imaging while the payment for CMR is influenced by a much broader range of imaging procedures. The commenter refers to the historical placement of CPT 75563 in APC 5593 (Level 3 Nuclear Medicine and Related Services)—before the CY 2017 APC restructuring—and how there is resource and clinical homogeneity between CMR and nuclear cardiac imaging. This is especially important, the commenter continues, because these codes include contrast-enhanced imaging and pharmacologic stress. The commenter notes that these services are paid approximately 40-60 percent less despite the commenter's belief that there is comparable or greater clinical resource intensity.
The commenter requested that we reassign CPT code 75561 to APC 5593 and reassign CPT code 75563 to APC 5594. The commenter also requested that we evaluate the appropriate placement of CPT code 75557 which is currently assigned to APC 5523 and CPT code 75559 which is currently assigned to APC 5524.
Response:
We thank the commenter for their thoughtful input. The OPPS payment rates were proposed based on available CY 2025 claims data. Our claims data shows that APC 5593 (Level 3 Nuclear Medicine and Related Services) has a geometric mean cost of approximately $1,433 which is significantly higher than the geometric mean costs of the cardiac MRI codes ($305 to $783).
As stated in last year's final rule (
90 FR 53567
), we do not believe that cardiac MRI with stress imaging is very similar to myocardial perfusion imaging just because both tests are performed under a stress protocol, and therefore should be assigned to a nuclear medicine APC. APC 5593 contains procedures that describe nuclear medicine tests, not MRI services. We continue to believe (and have stated in previous rulemaking), that MRI services should not be assigned to the nuclear medicine APCs (
81 FR 79630
and
90 FR 53567
).
In summary, after consideration of the public comment, we are finalizing our proposal without modification to maintain the APC assignments for the cardiac MRI codes for CY 2027. The final CY 2027 payment rates for these codes can be found in Addendum B to this final rule with comment period. In addition, we refer readers to Addendum D1 to this final rule with comment period for the status indicator definitions for all codes reported under the OPPS. Addenda B and D1 are available via the internet on the CMS website.

Cardiac computed tomography services are described by the following Category I CPT codes and have been effective since January 1, 2010:

For CY 2027, the OPPS payment rates were proposed based on available CY 2025 claims data for ratesetting. We note that CPT code 75572 has a geometric mean cost of $183 calculated using 41,211 single frequency claims; CPT code 75573 has a geometric mean cost of $234 calculated using 559 claims; and CPT code 75574 has a geometric mean cost of $227 calculated using 116,963 claims. For CY 2027, we proposed to maintain these codes to APC 5572 (Level 2 Imaging with Contrast) with a payment rate of around $400.
As a reminder to readers, we reassigned these codes to APC 5572 in CY 2025 because of the assumption that facilities would have chosen the cardiology revenue code if they had been able to versus the CT scan (035X) and Radiology Diagnostic (032X) revenue codes. We became aware of an edit (that we removed in December 2024) that was prohibiting hospitals from reporting these codes with a cardiology revenue code (048X) which maps to the cardiology cost center (03140). The cardiology cost center has a higher cost-to-charge ratio (CCR) than the imaging cost centers. Utilizing cost centers with lower CCRs results in a lower OPPS payment compared to utilizing cost centers with higher CCRs. With the edit no longer in place, hospitals are able to bill for cardiac CT services with whichever revenue code they believe is appropriate for these services, including cardiology revenue code 048X. For a full discussion of this issue, we refer readers to
89 FR 94057
through
94062
. We received public comments on these codes.
Comment:
We received numerous comments in support of maintaining the current APC assignment. Commenters requested that we continue to maintain the APC assignment while they continue their efforts to educate their providers and hospitals to change their billing practices. They note that there is continued hesitancy surrounding the selection of appropriate revenue codes because of `CT' in the coding descriptors. The revenue codes hospitals use to report cardiac CT
(
printed page 70388)
services materially affects whether OPPS payment accurately reflects the resources involved in furnishing them. Reporting cardiac CT services under cardiology revenue codes (048x) more accurately reflects the resources associated with furnishing the service. Additionally, a commenter requested that CMS issue sub-regulatory guidance and provider education confirming that cardiology revenue codes are appropriate to report for cardiac CT services, so that facility cost data and OPPS rate-setting better reflect the clinical resources used to provide the services.
Response:
We appreciate the commenters' support. Once again, we agree with commenters that effectuating change in any health system can be challenging. As we stated in the CY 2025 OPPS/ASC final rule, we will continue to monitor the claims data for these services, knowing that it may take a number of years before we see changes in the claims data.
As noted previously, commenters continue to request guidance that explicitly states that it is appropriate to use the cardiology revenue codes when billing for cardiac CT services. As a reminder to our readers and as we have previously stated, we do not provide specific coding guidance. We refer our readers to section 20.5 in Chapter 4 (Part B Hospital) of the Medicare Claims Processing Manual, “CMS does not instruct hospitals on the assignment of HCPCS codes to revenue codes for services provided under OPPS since hospitals' assignments of cost vary. Where explicit instructions are not provided, HOPDs should report their charges under the revenue code that will result in the charges being assigned to the same cost center to which the cost of those services are assigned in the cost report.” We have consistently stated that hospital outpatient facilities must determine the most appropriate cost center and revenue code for the cardiac CT codes (
87 FR 71849
,
88 FR 81664
, and
90 FR 53566
).
In summary for CY 2027, we are finalizing our proposal without modification and assigning CT codes 75572, 75573, and 75574 to APC 5572 (Level 2 Imaging with Contrast). The final CY 2027 payment rates for these codes can be found in Addendum B to this final rule with comment period. In addition, we refer readers to Addendum D1 to this final rule with comment period for the status indicator definitions for all codes reported under the OPPs. Addenda B and D1 are available via the internet on the CMS website.

We received several comments related to this proposal.
Comments:
Commenters supported the deletion of these C-codes but a couple of commenters requested that we create a new C-code to mirror CPT code 92930 (

(
printed page 70390)
coronary lesions with 2 or more coronary stents deployed in 2 or more coronary segments, or a bifurcation lesion requiring angioplasty and/or stenting in both the main artery and the side branch
) when two drug eluting stents are used in two or more distinct lesions. The commenters stated that without an equivalent C-code for this scenario, there would be a CPT/HCPCS mismatch.
Response:
We thank the commenters for their support to delete the previous C-codes. We disagree with commenters that a new C-code should be created to mirror CPT code 92930. The deleted C-codes were created when drug-eluting stents were novel and had significantly higher costs associated with them and we needed a mechanism to capture those costs. We believe that the gap between the costs of drug-eluting stents and bare metal stents are not as significant as they were over ten years ago when these C-codes were created.
In summary, after consideration of the public comments we received, we are finalizing our proposal without modification to delete the previous HCPCS C-codes and decline to create a C-code at this time to mirror CPT code 92930.

11. Dialysis-Related Amyloidosis (DRA) Treatment With LIXELLE® Apheresis Columns and Dialysis Technologies
LIXELLE® b2-microglobulinApheresis Column is indicated for use in the treatment of dialysis-related amyloidosis (DRA), a disease that affects people with end-stage renal disease (ESRD). DRA is a metabolic disorder from the failure of the kidney to filter and remove b2 microglobulin, typically from chronic hemodialysis (typically 5 years or longer). The LIXELLE® device is used in an apheresis procedure that selectively removes b2-microglobulin from circulating blood and is used in accordance with a physician prescription in conjunction with hemodialysis. It is intended to be used at each hemodialysis session (that is, frequency of treatment is expected to be 3 times per week). In March 2015, FDA approved a Humanitarian Device Exemption (HDE) application for LIXELLE® a Class III Humanitarian Use Device (HUD).
For CY 2027, there are currently no specific HCPCS or CPT codes that represent the service performed with the LIXELLE® apheresis device. We received public comments on this topic. The following is a summary of the comments we received and our responses.
Comment:
A commenter notes that access to LIXELLE® has been limited by the lack of a clear reimbursement pathway, and they urge CMS to clarify coverage in the OPPS Final Rule for the benefit of the small number of patients with DRA. The commenter states that the FDA recognizes that there continues to be no feasible alternative treatments for DRA in the United States, and that extensive clinical evidence supports LIXELLE® as reasonable and necessary for the treatment of DRA.
The commenter understands that CMS continues to evaluate how to facilitate Medicare reimbursement for treatments of medical devices that are administered during dialysis procedures but that are not “renal dialysis services” and supports a CMS policy clarification that such treatments and dialysis procedures that accompany them are appropriately reimbursed through OPPS benefit. The commenter reminded CMS
(
printed page 70392)
that the FDA further clarified that “qualified health care professionals such as physician assistants, nurse practitioner or registered nurses are qualified to supervise hemodialysis procedures” to alleviate previous clinical supervision concerns.
Another commenter supported the payment of dialysis technologies not included in the End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) bundle through the OPPS and urged CMS to assign an appropriate APC to facilitate payment for the apheresis procedure with LIXELLE® in the OPPS.
Response:
We appreciate the comments and continued interest regarding coverage and payment for medical device technologies used in conjunction with dialysis services, such as LIXELLE® for the treatment of DRA. We understand that DRA represents a serious complication for long-term dialysis patients and the need for effective treatment options. We continue to contemplate coverage pathways for innovative treatments that address unmet medical needs in the ESRD population and note this complex, ongoing issue is still under consideration.
We remind commenters that routine outpatient maintenance dialysis for End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) is not paid under the OPPS and because the treatment with Lixelle is used at each hemodialysis session (
e.g.,
routine maintenance dialysis), we do not believe that the OPPS is a viable option for payment for the DRA treatment with LIXELLE® at this time. We also recognize the challenges of ensuring appropriate payment pathways for innovative treatments that may be administered during dialysis but fall outside the definition of a renal dialysis service under § 413.171 and thus are not paid for under the ESRD PPS.
We will continue to evaluate the appropriate payment mechanisms for such technologies for future rulemaking.

15. Venous Mechanical Thrombectomy, CPT Code 37187 (APC 5193)

85 FR 85987
).
Comment:
A commenter requested that CMS reconsider the current methodology used to determine claims for ratesetting for CPT code 37187 and the proposed assignment of the code to APC 5193. The commenter opined that the current rate does not adequately reflect the reported geometric mean cost for the procedure and variation in the costs at the claim level. The commenter, using the growth in Medicare usage of venous thrombectomy and increased utilization of the hospital outpatient setting, asked CMS to consider whether the rate-setting claims adequately reflect current practice patterns and the adoption of technology, variation in coding, complexity of patients, and site-of-service trends, and to consider whether additional data or a different methodology would better determine accurate payments.
Response:
We appreciate the commenter's concerns regarding payment for CPT code 37187. CMS previously reassigned CPT 37187 from APC 5192 to APC 5193 for CY 2021 after finding that its geometric mean cost was comparable to other clinically related thrombectomy and endovascular services in APC 5193 (
85 FR 85987
). We reviewed the most updated claims data available for CY 2027 rate setting and continue to believe that APC 5193 appropriately reflects the clinical characteristics and relative resource costs of CPT code 37187. Under the OPPS, payment rates are established at the APC level based on the geometric mean cost of all applicable services assigned to the APC based on clinical and cost similarity. The number of claims used to calculate the geometric mean cost for CPT code 37187 represents claims remaining after application of the comprehensive APC rate-setting methodology and should not be interpreted as total Medicare utilization. Under that methodology, qualifying higher-cost combinations involving CPT code 37187 receive a complexity adjustment and are reassigned to the next higher-level endovascular APC. Consequently, those complexity-adjusted claims are removed from the cost calculation for CPT code 37187 in APC 5193 and included separately in APC 5194. We further note that most claims containing CPT code 37187 that were available were used for OPPS ratesetting purposes, whether for the code itself or as part of a code combination qualifying for complexity adjustment.
Although the commenter identified variation among CPT code 37187 claims, this variation does not, by itself, demonstrate that the claims are inaccurate or that the service is inappropriately assigned. Moreover, we believe that some of that variation is a reflection of the varying practice patterns in the claims containing codes, most of which we are using in our OPPS ratesetting process. We received public comments on this proposal. The following is a summary of the comments we received and our responses.
Comment:
A commenter, the manufacturer, requested reassignment of 0779T from APC 5723 (Level 3 Diagnostic Tests and Related Services) to APC 5724 (Level 4 Diagnostic Tests and Related Services). The commenter stated that APC 5723 is inadequate to cover the costs of the hospital's supplies, equipment, and staff needed to provide this service. The commenter cited the acquisition of continuous physiologic data across three gastrointestinal organ regions for up to six days and the required post-acquisition processing for CPT 0779T as justification for the higher-level APC assignment. The commenter claimed clinical and resource coherence to CPT code 91035 (Esophagus, gastroesophageal reflux test; with mucosal attached telemetry pH
(
printed page 70396)
electrode placement, recording, analysis and interpretation) as a multi-day, multi-organ ambulatory diagnostic.
Response:
We thank the commenter for their comment. After further review and additional discussion with our medical officers, we are finalizing our proposal without modification to continue to assign CPT code 0779T to APC 5723 for CY 2027. CMS continues to believe that assigning CPT code 0779T to APC 5723 is supported. More specifically, CMS believes CPT code 0779T shares more clinical and resource similarities with the services assigned to APC 5723 than those assigned to APC 5724, which are generally more complicated and invasive services. In regard to the commenter's reference to similarities to CPT code 91035, we note that while CPT code 0779T and CPT code 91035 are both diagnostic gastroenterology tests used to track physiological activity inside the digestive tract, we believe the invasiveness of the upper endoscopy included in CPT code 91035 requires more resources than an external wearable patch system described by CPT code 0779T. We will continue to monitor the claims data and update the payment rate in future rulemaking based on the available claims.
The final CY 2027 payment rates can be found in Addendum B to this final rule with comment period via the internet on the CMS website. In addition, we refer readers to Addendum D1 to this final rule with comment period for the status indicator meanings for all codes reported under the OPPS. Comment:

Response:
We thank the commenter for the information regarding the clinical and operational resources associated with the CT colonography (CTC). We recognize that CTC involves bowel preparation, oral contrast administration, insufflation, multiple image acquisitions, image postprocessing and technologist involvement. We reviewed CPT code 74263 and noted that the GMC is $88 based on 692 single frequency claims.

22. Breast Imaging Service Performed With QT Scanner, CPT Code 1079T (APC 5522)
Effective October 1, 2026, CPT code 1079T (placeholder code X579T)
(3D quantitative transmission water bath volumetric ultrasound tomography, breast, with augmentative algorithmic derivation of breast tissue composition (ie, fibroglandular volume), bilateral, with physician or other qualified health care professional interpretation and report)
describes the breast imaging service performed with QT Scanner. The device uses a 360-degree moving transducer to generate quantitative 3D breast images. The QT Scanner 2000 Model A is indicated to provide reflection-mode and transmission-mode breast images and calculates fibroglandular tissue volume (breast density), and is “not intended to be used as a replacement for screening mammography.”
For CY 2027, we proposed to assign CPT code 1079T to status indicator “E1” because we did not believe the QT Scanner service would fall under an existing benefit category.
We received a public comment on this proposal. The following is a summary of the comment we received and our response.
Comment:
A commenter, the manufacturer of QT Scanner, requested that we revise the proposed “E1” status indicator to status indicator “S” for CPT code 1079T and assign the code to a new technology APC. Per the commenter, physician-ordered diagnostic use of the QT Scanner falls within an existing Medicare benefit category under section 1861(s)(3) and section 1861(s)(2)(B) of the Social Security Act, and NCD 220.5 (Ultrasound Diagnostic Procedures (Effective May 22, 2007)) provides coverage either as breast sonography under Category I or as an unenumerated diagnostic ultrasound procedure subject to local MAC discretion under Section D. The commenter also cited FDA clearance of the QT Scanner 2000 Model
(
printed page 70398)
A (K253898) and CPT's creation of the Category III CPT code as support for the existence of a diagnostic use distinct from screening.
Response:
After reviewing the comment, we agree, on a narrow basis, that assignment of status indicator E1 is not appropriate for CPT code 1079T. We agree that physician-ordered use of a QT Scanner to evaluate a specific clinical finding could be capable of falling within the existing diagnostic ultrasound benefit category described in NCD 220.5 Ultrasound Diagnostic Procedures, consistent with CMS's treatment of other forms of breast sonography. In the event this code is covered, and determined to be reasonable and necessary, we believe an appropriate APC assignment for CPT code 1079T is APC 5522 (Level 2 Imaging without Contrast), based on similar codes in that APC series, for example CPT code 76641
(Ultrasound, breast, unilateral or bilateral, real-time with image documentation, complete).
Therefore, for CY 2027, in response to the commenter, we are revising our proposal in this final rule and assigning CPT code 1079T to APC 5522 with status indicator “S.”
As we have consistently stated in past OPPS/ASC final rules with comment period (see, for example,
87 FR 71879
and
88 FR 81660
through
81661
), the fact that a drug, device, procedure or service is assigned a HCPCS code and a payment rate under the OPPS does not imply coverage by the Medicare program, but indicates only how the product, procedure, or service may be paid if covered by the program. Coverage of a claim where the QT Scanner is used would require an independent showing, made at the time the claim is adjudicated, that the service was reasonable and necessary for the individual beneficiary under section 1862(a)(1)(A) of the Act, ordered by a physician to address a specific diagnostic question.
While our decision to finalize payment rests on the plausible diagnostic use of this technology within the existing framework of NCD 220.5, under current rules, use of the QT Scanner would not be covered by Medicare as a screening service. Coverage of breast ultrasonography as a screening service would require either a statutory change or a qualifying recommendation from the United States Preventive Services Task Force under section 1861(ddd) of the Act. Neither condition currently exists. Therefore, claims for QT Scanner where the service is furnished for routine screening of asymptomatic beneficiaries would not currently be covered. Additionally, we clarify that the indication for the FDA-cleared device, itself, does not support the use of the QT Scanner device for breast cancer screening.
In summary, we are not finalizing our proposal to assign CPT code 1079T to status indicator “E1” as proposed. In response to the commenter, for CY 2027, we are assigning CPT code 1079T to APC 5522 and status indicator “S.” Refer to Table 36 for the final CY 2027 OPPS APC and status indicator assignments for CPT code 1079T. The final CY 2027 payment rates for this code can be found in Addendum B to this final rule with comment period. In addition, we refer readers to Addendum D1 to this final rule with comment period for the status indicator definitions for all codes reported under the OPPS. Addenda B and D1 are available via the internet on the CMS website.

Transcutaneous Magnetic Peripheral Nerve Stimulation is intended to stimulate peripheral nerves for relief of chronic intractable pain, post‐traumatic pain, post‐surgical pain and/or for relief of chronic painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy in the lower extremities for patients 18 and older. CPT code 0766T (Transcutaneous magnetic stimulation by focused low-frequency electromagnetic pulse, peripheral nerve, with identification and marking of the treatment location, including noninvasive electroneurographic localization (nerve conduction localization), when performed; first nerve) became effective January 1, 2023. For CY 2025, CPT code 0766T was reassigned to APC 5722 (Level 2 Diagnostic Tests and Related Services) with the status indicator “S” (Significant Procedures, Not Discounted when Multiple. Paid under OPPS; separate APC payment). There are no claims available for CPT code 0766T in CY 2025. For CY 2027, we proposed to continue assigning CPT code 0766T to APC 5722.
CPT code 0767T (Transcutaneous magnetic stimulation by focused low-frequency electromagnetic pulse, peripheral nerve, with identification and marking of the treatment location, including noninvasive electroneurographic localization (nerve conduction localization), when performed; each additional nerve (list separately in addition to code for primary procedure)) became effective January 1, 2023 and assigned status indicator “N” (packaged). CPT code 0767T is an add-on code and we proposed to continue assignment of status indicator “N” for this code for CY 2026 (
90 FR 53583
).
We note that at the August 24, 2026, HOP Panel Meeting, a presentation was made requesting (1) the reassignment of 0766T from APC 5722 to APC 5724 (Level 4 Diagnostic Tests and Related Services) and (2) reassignment of the status indicator for 0767T from “N” to “S” (Significant Procedures, Not Discounted when Multiple. Paid under OPPS; separate APC payment). The Panel made no recommendations on these requests.
We received 4 comments on this proposal. The following is a summary of the comments we received and our responses.
Comment:
All commenters requested CPT code 0766T be reassigned to APC 5724 (Level 4 Diagnostic Tests and Related Services), claiming that CPT code 0766T is not clinically similar and does not use comparable resources to other services in APC 5722. All commenters also stated that it is necessary to change the status indicator from “N” to “S” for CPT code 0767T because the additional nerve stimulations require the physician to reposition the device, identify and map a separate nerve target, establish appropriate stimulation parameters, and deliver treatment to that additional anatomical target. All commenters requested that CMS follow the 2025 HOP Panel recommendations to reassign 0766T to APC 5724 and reassign the 0767T status indicator to “S” (Significant Procedures, Not Discounted
(
printed page 70400)
when Multiple. Paid under OPPS; separate APC payment).
Response:
We disagree that CPT code 0766T is comparable, clinically and in resource costs, to the services assigned to APC 5724. We continue to believe CPT code 0766T is more comparable, clinically and from a resource cost perspective, to CPT code 90867 (Therapeutic repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (tms) treatment; initial, including cortical mapping, motor threshold determination, delivery and management), and CPT code 90868 (Therapeutic repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (tms) treatment; subsequent delivery and management, per session), which are assigned to APC 5722 (Level 2 Diagnostic Tests and Related Services), because these services share similar magnetic stimulation and nerve localization processes.
We note that CPT code 0767T is an add-on code. Add-on codes are always performed in addition to the primary service or procedure and not reported as a stand-alone code. As specified under regulation
42 CFR 419.2(b)(18)
, add-on codes are generally packaged under the OPPS, and payment for the codes are bundled with the primary codes. Consequently, CPT code 0767T is not paid separately under the OPPS and its payment is packaged into payment for the primary code.
After consideration of the public comments we received, we are finalizing our proposed APC assignment and status indicators for CPT codes 0766T and 0767T without modification.
We refer readers to Addendum B to this final rule with comment period for the payment rates for all codes reportable under the OPPS. Addendum B is available via the internet on the CMS website.

Comment:
We received two comments supporting the creation of these codes, their APC assignments, and the fact that we made them effective retroactive to January 1, 2026. A commenter suggested that CMS delay finalizing these codes, as they believe that the AMA CPT Editorial Panel is creating new HGNS codes. Another commenter requested that we reassign C-code C8011 to a New Technology APC suggesting that APC 5465 (Level 5 Neurostimulator and Related Procedures) does not adequately account for the device costs and hospital resources required to perform this procedure.
Response:
We thank the commenters for their input and support for the creation of these codes. We appreciate the fact that a commenter has suggested that we wait to finalize the HCPCS C-codes we created that describe the HGNS procedures; however, we want to address the coding and billing issues that surround these newer technologies that are not described by existing codes. If and when new CPT codes are created that describe these newer HGNS procedures, we will review the new codes and determine if maintaining the HCPCS C-codes are necessary. Regarding the APC assignments for these C-codes, we believe that the proposed APC assignments are appropriate, as we crosswalked the new C-codes to the existing coding for the HGNS procedures. We do not believe that it is appropriate to assign C8011 to a New Technology APC at this time without having adequate claims data to support the reassignment. We review, on an annual basis, the APC assignments for all services and items paid under the OPPS based on our analysis of the latest claims data and review of the clinical characteristics of the procedure.
In summary, after consideration of the public comments we received, we are finalizing the proposed APC assignments for the C-codes noted previously without modification. 31. Scalp Cooling Preparation and Pre-Cooling Service, CPT 97007-97009 (APC 1494)
Scalp cooling is a service furnished during chemotherapy to prevent or minimize hair loss, a common side effect of chemotherapy treatment for cancer. The service is furnished in two parts. On a different date of service than the chemotherapy session, the patient's head is measured and a scalp cooling cap is individually fitted to the patient. On the day of chemotherapy administration, the service includes a precooling and preparation period of approximately 30 minutes prior to chemotherapy initiation, placement and maintenance of the cooling cap during chemotherapy infusion, and a post-infusion cooling period following discontinuation of chemotherapy, as clinically appropriate.

97007—Mechanical scalp cooling, including individual cap supply with head measurement, fitting, and patient education.
97008—Mechanical scalp cooling; including hair preparation, individual cap placement, therapy initiation, and precooling period).
97009—Mechanical scalp cooling; provided after discontinuation of chemotherapy, each 30 minutes (List separately in addition to code for primary procedure).

Therefore, we packaged payment for CPT codes 97008 and 97009 with the primary chemotherapy service performed at the same time (
90 FR 53597

We received public comments on this proposal. The following is a summary of the comments we received and our responses.
Comment:

(
printed page 70405)
session. 36. Evacuation of Meibomian Glands, Using Heat Delivered Through Wearable, Open-Eye Eyelid Treatment Devices and Manual Gland Expression, Bilateral CPT 0563T (APC 5501)
CPT code 0563T describes evacuation of meibomian glands, using heat delivered through wearable, open-eye eyelid treatment devices and manual gland expression, bilateral. TearCare® is a technology-enabled interventional therapy for meibomian gland disease (MGD) and dry eye disease (DED) that continuously heats all four eyelids to a therapeutic temperature to melt or liquefy hardened oil obstructions in the meibomian glands, followed by physician-performed manual evacuation of the glands.
DED is a chronic affliction of the ocular surface. In the human eye, meibum, aqueous, and mucus form the three layers of tear film, which is the fluid that keeps the eye moist and serves the critical function of protecting the cornea. Meibomian glands are important oil producing glands located within each of the four eyelids. When healthy, these glands produce a clear liquid oil called meibum, which is expressed with every blink, coats the tear with oil, and prevents the tear from evaporating prematurely and exposing the cornea. In patients with MGD, the meibomian glands become diseased and inflamed and the meibum hardens. Obstructed meibomian glands cannot produce healthy new liquid meibum, leaving the tear uncoated and resulting in accelerated tear evaporation and an exposed cornea. This evaporative cascade is the leading cause of dry eye disease.
In the 2027 ASC/OPPS proposed rule, we proposed to continue to assign CPT code 0563T to status indicator “Q1” and APC 5733 (Level 3 Minor Procedures) with proposed payment rate of $66.91.
We received several public comments related to our proposal. The following is a summary of the comments we received.

The commenters requested that we reassign CPT code 0563T from APC 5733 to APC 5503 (Level 3 Extraocular, Repair and Plastic Eye Procedures) with status indicator “J1” and proposed payment rate of $2,808.31. TearCare® requires specialized capital equipment, single-use bilateral treatment components, treatment of all four eyelids, clinical staff and treatment-room resources, followed by physician-performed manual evacuation of the meibomian glands. The single-use treatment components alone have a cost
(
printed page 70408)
that substantially exceeds the proposed APC 5733 payment.
They also pointed out that TearCare® is performed predominantly in the physician-office setting, where utilization does not generate an OPPS facility claim. Therefore, the limited HOPD claims reflect where TearCare® is currently performed rather than the resources required to furnish the procedure. They stated they do not believe these limited claims provide a representative basis for determining the appropriate APC assignment for CPT 0563T and those limited claims could have been filed in error. This is particularly important because the current APC payment, in their opinion, does not adequately recognize the resources required to furnish the procedure in the HOPD and may create a barrier for providers seeking to offer TearCare® to Medicare beneficiaries in other settings of care.
According to one of the commenters, the procedure requires dedicated equipment (SmartHub); bilateral, single-use Smartlid devices, a tool to clear glands, and additional supplies; in addition to clinical labor time for pre-service, intraservice, and post-service activities involving approximately 60 minutes. 37. Application of Rigid Total Contact Leg Cast, CPT Code 29445 (APC 5102)
CPT code 29445 describes a procedure of applying a Total Contact Leg Cast. Total contact casting (“TCC”—which is pressure offloading) is an integral part of the standard of care for diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) management, alongside with vascular management, infection management, and sharp debridement, deemed as the “VIPS” of DFU care. The use of TCC is often associated with higher healing rates, faster healing times, lower infection rates, and fewer amputations.
TCC is commonly applied after a debridement or grafting procedure during the same office or clinic visit to protect the wound site from ongoing pressure, which could further delay healing.
In the CY 2027 ASC/OPPS proposed rule, we proposed to continue to assign CPT code 29445 to status indicator “T” (Procedure or service, multiple procedure reduction applies; with a separate APC payment under OPPS) and APC 5102 (Level 2 Strapping and Cast Application) with proposed payment rate of $331.21.
At the August 24, 2026, HOP Panel Meeting, a presenter advised the Panel to request that CMS reassign CPT code 29445 (
Application of rigid total contact leg cast
) to status indicator “S” (Procedure or Service, Not Discounted When Multiple; with a separate APC payment under OPPS). Based on the information presented at the meeting, the Panel recommended that CMS make that reassignment.
We received one comment related to CPT code 29445.
Comment:
The commenter stated that CPT coding guidance allows for debridement (CPT codes 11042-11047, 97597-97598) as well as the application of CTPs (CPT codes 15271-15278) on the same date of service as the application of TCC (CPT code 29445). The cast improves the ability of the wound to heal. If a wound debridement is performed (CPT codes 11042-11047, 97597-97598), any primary or secondary dressing materials used to cover the wound would be included in the debridement and would not be separately reported. However, a TCC is not considered a wound dressing and is not included in the debridement procedure. Therefore, the cast application should be coded in addition to the code for the appropriate level of debridement, if performed, and should be assigned to status indicator “S” because the application of a TCC is labor intensive and the cost of the product is not insignificant.
Response:
We thank the commenter for their input. Per our evaluation of the service and an input from our medical advisors, we determined that there are other clinical procedures that involve an application of cast, such as an application of short leg cast, described by CPT code 29405 or an Unna boot that
(
printed page 70409)
is also used for leg ulcer treatment, that is described by CPT code 29580, that are assigned to status indicator “T”. Therefore, we believe that status indicator “T” is appropriately assigned to TCC. As a result, we are maintaining our status indicator assignment as proposed for CY 2027.

We received a public comment on this proposal. The following is a summary of the comment we received and our response.
Comment:
A commenter stated that the assignment of CPT code 28740 to APC 5114 may represent a violation of the 2 times rule, which may impede access to care for beneficiaries. The commenter recommended that CMS consider a volume threshold of 500 single major claims (or the existing greater or equal to 99 claims that
(
printed page 70410)
constitute greater than or equal to the 2 percent criterion) as the standard for designating an item or service “significant” for purposes of the 2 times rule. The commenter requested that we reassign CPT code 28740 to APC 5114 (Level 5 Musculoskeletal Procedures) to resolve the alleged 2 times rule violation.
Response:
We appreciate the commenter's input. As discussed in section III.B. of this final rule with comment period, for purposes of reviewing APCs for determining violations of the two-times rule, we consider a procedure code cost significant when it has more than 1,000 single-major claims or when it has more than 99 single major claims and accounts for at least 2 percent of the single major claims used to establish the APC cost.
Based on our review of the updated claims data available for this final rule with comment period, CPT code 28740 has a geometric mean cost of approximately $12,571 based on 549 single claims. However, these claims do not meet the 2 percent threshold of claims used to establish ratesetting for APC 5114. Therefore, CPT code 28740 does not meet the significance threshold used in our evaluation of the two-times rule. The lowest-cost significant procedure in APC 5114 has a geometric mean cost of approximately $5,862.49, while the highest-cost significant procedure has a geometric mean cost of approximately $10,510.96. Consequently, we did not identify a violation of the two-times rule for APC 5114.
After consideration of the public comment, we are finalizing our proposal without modification to assign CPT code 28740 to APC 5114 with status indicator “J1” for CY 2027. The final CY 2027 payment rates for this code can be found in Addendum B to this final rule with comment period. We received public comments on this proposal. The following is a summary of the comments we received and our response.
Comment:
Commenters requested that CMS reconsider the proposed assignment of HCPCS code G0552 (Supply of digital mental health treatment device and initial education and onboarding, per course of treatment that augments a behavioral therapy plan) to APC 5012 (Clinic Visits and Related Services). Commenters stated that the assignment of HCPCS code G0552 to APC 5012 does not appropriately reflect the clinical characteristics or hospital resources associated with furnishing a DMHT device.

Commenters explained that DMHT devices deliver a therapeutic intervention to treat or alleviate a mental health condition, whereas RPM and RTM devices generally monitor a patient's status or response to treatment. Commenters also stated that the device supply for HCPCS code G0552 is furnished for an entire course of treatment, rather than being separately reported on a recurring basis.
Commenters further stated that the hospital costs associated with furnishing DMHT devices substantially exceed the payment rate for APC 5012. Commenters also stated that CMS's proposed payment policy for Software as a Medical Service (SaMS) supports recognizing hospital expenditures for access to proprietary software as a resource cost under the OPPS, even though DMHT devices are not included within the proposed definition of SaMS.

Response:
We thank the commenters for their recommendations and the information provided regarding the clinical characteristics and costs associated with furnishing DMHT devices. We continue to believe that APC 5012 (Clinic Visits and Related Services) is the most appropriate APC assignment for HCPCS code G0552 at this time. As discussed in in the CY 2025 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (
89 FR 94087
through
94088
), we believe that the DMHT services described by HCPCS codes G0552, G0553, and G0554 are clinically similar to other services assigned to APC 5012, and we believe that maintaining these services within the same APC continues to be appropriate based on the information currently available to us.
We acknowledge the commenters' concerns regarding the costs associated with the DMHT device included in HCPCS code G0552 and appreciate the additional cost information submitted by the commenters. However, we do not believe that the information submitted provides a sufficient basis at this time to reassign HCPCS code G0552 to APC 5723 or APC 5735, or to establish a new Level 4 Health and Behavioral Services APC.
As additional claims data become available for HCPCS code G0552, we will continue to evaluate the clinical and resource characteristics of the service and consider whether a different APC assignment may be appropriate in future rulemaking.
